title: the DSG cultures of the underdark

banner.title: THE DSG CULTURES OF THE UNDERDARK, R532: printed pp. 73-74 (pdf 74-75) - the third DM-section child: the values and objectives frame (the races relying less on trade and interaction than the surface races, the environment forcibly segregating them; trade governed more often by proximity than by alignment - an evil race more likely to trade with a nearby neutral race than a distant evil one; and the monster-encyclopedia referral), and the eight race write-ups: the drow (the strongly matriarchal society with females holding all power in government, military and home; the Lolth worship with the 6th-level-and-higher testing and the drider failures; the spider-like scorpions, pedipalp and solifugud; the web-pattern buildings with the traps channeling prey to the center; the aged-only cannibalism under population pressure; the treaty-breaking making alliances reluctant; and the long-term objective of ruling all subterranean races and controlling underworld access), the kuo-toa (the race past its prime struggling to retain its holdings, its inability to cooperate making it susceptible to conquest; the Sea Mother worship as the one unifying element with the holy-war dream; the 5% insanity breeding the monitor class; and the slave-acquiring brute force, treachery or barter), the duergar (the disciplined and orderly evil allowing dominance; the mountain-and-hill-dwarf kinship in mining and metal-and-stone work; the fiendish imprisoning traps with slow painful deaths; the slave labor with complete disregard for welfare; the mercilessness and torture love; the extermination over driving off to eliminate reprisal; and the sculpture-and-metalworking craft trade for slaves and devices), the mind flayers (the aboleth the only non-hostile race with the sinister-connection legends; the brain hunger leaving bodies to the scavengers; the racial quest to douse the fires of the sun itself; the probability-travel escape from difficult odds; the rigidly psionic-ranked society with slave labor and slave food; the life-form experiments with their hostile hybrids; and the immunity-bought-with-slaves trade and the temporary aboleth pacts), the aboleth (the most alien culture from the human point of view, coldly ruthless with torture serving no rational purpose; the intended complete control of the underworld beginning with the underground waters - the main reason for the kuo-toan waning; the obscene mind flayer pacts with the illithid as a temporary tool; the godless reverence of the greater aboleth, one to six per city at four times the size and Hit Dice, the repositories of the alien knowledge; and the remote casually-guarded slave cities), the derro (the small savage bands never in large communities, raiding near the surface; the chaos and intraracial violence; the stealing over working and the short-lived duergar and drow pacts; and the 20-year savant war cycle ending in utter defeat but recovered by the high reproductive rate), and the cloakers (the true children of the earth with the Elemental Plane of Earth ties; the most intelligent of their type over the lurkers, miners, trappers and mantari servants; the violence answering all contact attempts; the toolless structureless culture with its instinctive community sense; and the guerrilla warfare and kin-sacrificing defense)
banner.provenance: the DSG scan (archive.org item advanced-dungeons-dragons-1st-edition), pdf = printed + 1; the text read from the IA djvu OCR (djvu.txt lines ~9268-9460) with the pdf Acrobat-Capture layer as the second read (idx 172-174 = the printed pp. 73-74 windows; the odd image-heavy interleaves hold no text in Capture); the compiled-tables appendix has no reprint of this prose. A CLEAN-READ ROUND: both machine reads agree on every load-bearing number - the 6th-level Lolth test, the 5% kuo-toan insanity, the one-to-six greater aboleth at four times the size and Hit Dice, and the 20-year derro war cycle; the only garbles are the standing glyph classes (the FIEND FOLIO and Monster Manual II titles garbled in both layers - the references settled by the chapter context, Monster Manual II for duergar, aboleth, derro and cloakers, the Fiend Folio for drow and kuo-toa, the Monster Manual for illithids). SEAMS: the Fiend Folio drow and kuo-toa, the Monster Manual II duergar, aboleth, derro and cloakers, the Monster Manual mind flayer, the R530-R531 environment and geography rounds (the kuo-toan waning and the water dominion), and the R503 re-grain. Nothing auto-credits.
banner.sentinel: A prose round: no tables pin. The numbers pin as consts per the R508 convention: the 6th-level Lolth test, the 5% kuo-toan insanity, the one-to-six greater aboleth per city, the four-times size-and-Hit-Dice multiplier, and the 20-year derro war cycle. The rest pins as prose bools: the values-and-objectives frame and the eight race write-ups (drow, kuo-toa, duergar, mind flayers, aboleth, derro, cloakers). The FF/MM/MMII/R530-R531/R503 seams are noted; nothing auto-credits.

consts.name: dncuDrowTestLevel
consts.comment: drow of 6th level or higher are often tested by Lolth; those that fail become driders - half-drow, half-spider outcasts found around the fringes of drow realms.

consts.name: dncuKuoToaInsanePct
consts.comment: as many as 5% of all men-fish suffer from mental imbalance and are prone to go berserk at the slightest provocation - the cause of the kuo-toan monitor class.

consts.name: dncuGreaterAbolethMax
consts.comment: each aboleth city has from one to six greater aboleth - huge, loathsome creatures commanding the deep respect of the others.

consts.name: dncuGreaterAbolethMult
consts.comment: the greater aboleth can be up to four times the size and Hit Dice of a normal aboleth; they are the repositories of the vast alien knowledge collected by the race.

consts.name: dncuDerroWarYears
consts.comment: once every 20 or so years the derro savants unite their race and embark upon a vicious war of raid and plunder - always ending in utter defeat, but the high reproductive rate allows recovery.

bools.name: dncuSegregatedLessTrade
bools.comment: the Underdark races rely less on trade and interaction than surface races - the underground environment forcibly segregates the creatures living there; some trade occurs among them, and with the surface less frequently.

bools.name: dncuProximityOverAlignment
bools.comment: trade is more often governed by proximity than by alignment: an evil race would most likely trade with a nearby neutral race than with a more distant evil race.

bools.name: dncuMonsterGuideReferral
bools.comment: each major race is covered in detail in TSRs monster encyclopedia; this section expands on the material previously presented, especially as regards the societies and cultures of these races.

bools.name: dncuDrowMatriarchal
bools.comment: drow society has developed along strongly matriarchal lines - females hold all positions of power and responsibility in government, the military and at home; males are effective fighters and can become low-level magic-users or clerics, but are rarely encountered unless under the command of higher-ranking females.

bools.name: dncuDrowLolth
bools.comment: the drow worship the spider god Lolth and many aspects of their culture reflect this - spider-like creatures such as scorpions, pedipalp and solifugud commonly found among their communities.

bools.name: dncuDrowWebPattern
bools.comment: the drow emulate spider characteristics: their buildings and cavern networks are often created in a web pattern, with traps channeling creatures toward the center of the web.

bools.name: dncuDrowCannibalism
bools.comment: in times of severe population pressure the drow practice cannibalism, weeding out the weaker members - the victims always the aged, since the safety of the young is very important to the drow.

bools.name: dncuDrowTreatiesBroken
bools.comment: the drow culture is perhaps the most widespread and firmly entrenched of all underground cultures; the drow make treaties when it serves their interests but are quick to break them if the terms no longer seem advantageous - making other races reluctant to enter alliances with them.

bools.name: dncuDrowRuleObjective
bools.comment: the long-term drow objective is to rule over all other subterranean races and control all access to and from the underworld - unlikely in the near future, but the drow endorse any proposal moving them closer without endangering their current dominant position.

bools.name: dncuKuoToaPastPrime
bools.comment: the kuo-toa have passed their prime as a race and struggle simply to retain their holdings and some degree of cultural integrity - many communities remain, but their inability to cooperate in the face of threats makes them susceptible to conquest by more disciplined races.

bools.name: dncuKuoToaSeaMother
bools.comment: worship of the Sea Mother is the one unifying element of kuo-toan culture; a few of the oldest and wisest clerics dream of joining the chaotic and feuding factions into one mighty army and carrying forth a great holy war in her name - not likely, but the believers constantly work the plan forward.

bools.name: dncuKuoToaMonitors
bools.comment: the dramatic decline of the race has resulted in the high insanity incidence - and the monitor class of elite kuo-toans charged with controlling the members of their race that succumb.

bools.name: dncuKuoToaSlaveTrade
bools.comment: kuo-toans rarely trade with other races, having no industries and little to offer - but they are always interested in acquiring slaves and will work out any means to do so: brute force, treachery, or bartering a rare useful item.

bools.name: dncuDuergarDisciplinedEvil
bools.comment: the duergar, or gray ones, practice their evil in a disciplined and orderly fashion - allowing the race to prosper and dominate where more numerous creatures have failed; hard workers and tenacious combatants.

bools.name: dncuDuergarDwarfKin
bools.comment: the duergar culture resembles that of their higher cousins the mountain and hill dwarves: all rely heavily on mining, all skilled at working metals and stone; the gray dwarves are particularly adept at fiendish traps that imprison unwary prey and inflict slow, painful deaths.

bools.name: dncuDuergarSlaves
bools.comment: the duergar differ from their cousins in the frequent employment of slave labor and their complete disregard for the welfare of those slaves.

bools.name: dncuDuergarMerciless
bools.comment: arrayed for battle the duergar make a formidable force, known for complete mercilessness on the battlefield and their love of torture - captives unsuitable for slavery put to death in the most fiendish, macabre and time-consuming methods imaginable.

bools.name: dncuDuergarExterminate
bools.comment: the duergar seem to have no major ambitions of conquest, but fight fiercely to preserve what they have and to gain any appealing subterranean portion - usually where precious metals or gems are found outside their realms; they prefer to exterminate their foes rather than drive them off, eliminating threats of reprisal.

bools.name: dncuDuergarCraftTrade
bools.comment: many duergar become skilled craftsmen, particularly in sculpture and metalworking, trading their work with neighboring races for slaves and technological devices beyond their capabilities.

bools.name: dncuIllithidAbolethLink
bools.comment: the mind flayers are as alien and evil a race as exists in the Underdark, with the possible exception of the aboleth - the only other race toward whom the illithid are not actively hostile; ancient legends suggest a sinister connection between the two.

bools.name: dncuIllithidBrainHunger
bools.comment: the mind flayers do not pursue expansion or subjugation; any human, humanoid or demi-human unlucky enough to fall into their tentacles soon loses his brain to satisfy their fiendish hunger, his body left to the plentiful subterranean scavengers.

bools.name: dncuIllithidDouseSun
bools.comment: the mind flayer racial goal: loathing daylight and hating the confining chambers, they quest to destroy that which bars them from the surface world - to douse the fires of the sun itself, their genius-level Intelligence and psionic powers giving hope of someday achieving it.

bools.name: dncuIllithidPracticalRetreat
bools.comment: the mind flayers are a formidable military force, but if a battle goes against them they use their probability travel psionic ability to escape - far too practical to fight against difficult odds.

bools.name: dncuIllithidPsionicStatus
bools.comment: mind flayer society is rigidly organized, with status assigned according to psionic ability; slaves of all human and humanoid races are employed for most physical tasks and used as food.

bools.name: dncuIllithidHybrids
bools.comment: the illithid experiment with the development of life forms: their communities are surrounded by unidentifiable crosses between humans and loathsome monsters - slow, stupid and horrible, but often endowed with savagery, poison or other special features, and bearing no love for their creators.

bools.name: dncuIllithidImmunityTrade
bools.comment: mind flayers trade very little, needing few material possessions; other races buy immunity from their raids by providing a steady supply of slaves, and the mind flayers and aboleth occasionally enter temporary truces or pacts of cooperation to achieve some mutual goal - the subjugation of a weak community, for example.

bools.name: dncuAbolethColdlyRuthless
bools.comment: from a human point of view the aboleth are doubtless the most alien underground culture: actions nearly always calculated to advance their race with no regard for others; not interested in torture since it serves no rational purpose, but quick to kill any creature unlikely to serve as a useful slave.

bools.name: dncuAbolethWaterDominion
bools.comment: the aboleth intend to eventually gain complete control over the realms of the underworld; most effective in water, they first attempt to hold sway over all underground lakes, rivers and seas - their growing power one of the main reasons for the waning of the kuo-toan race.

bools.name: dncuAbolethIllithidTool
bools.comment: the aboleth occasionally enter obscene pacts with the mind flayers, always to the detriment of some hapless race - but the illithid will also be exterminated when their time comes; for now the aboleth use them as a convenient tool.

bools.name: dncuAbolethNoGod
bools.comment: the aboleth are not known to worship any god, but huge and loathsome examples of the species command deep respect - the greater aboleth, the repositories of the vast alien knowledge collected by the race.

bools.name: dncuAbolethRemoteCities
bools.comment: aboleth society is well ordered, the position of each individual rigidly defined; numerous slaves populate the cities, only casually guarded since the cities are usually so remote that escape is impossible.

bools.name: dncuDerroChaoticRaiders
bools.comment: the savage little derro are found in many places throughout the Underdark but never in large communities, often living near enough to the surface to raid for slaves and food there; their society is very chaotic and intraracial violence is commonplace.

bools.name: dncuDerroStealNotTrade
bools.comment: the derro perform little work and thus do not trade much with other races - they prefer to steal the possessions of others rather than make anything themselves; occasionally they enter an uneasy alliance with the duergar or the drow, but these pacts are always short lived and usually end in violence.

bools.name: dncuCloakerChildrenOfEarth
bools.comment: the cloakers are referred to as the true children of the earth - probably native to the Prime Plane but with strong ties to the Elemental Plane of Earth; they are the most intelligent variety of their type, which includes lurkers, miners, trappers and mantari, the others often accompanying them seemingly as servants.

bools.name: dncuCloakerViolence
bools.comment: cloakers resist all contact with other races - attempts to deal with them always result in violence and bloodshed.

bools.name: dncuCloakerNoTools
bools.comment: cloaker culture appears to have little organization: they neither use tools nor build permanent structures, and when danger threatens a community each cloaker seems to sense what it should do to further the best interests of the community.

bools.name: dncuCloakerGuerrilla
bools.comment: cloaker territories are easily conquered by organized foes, but savage guerrilla warfare often convinces the conquerors to relinquish their gains; cloakers sacrifice their less-intelligent kin in great numbers to defeat an enemy.
